newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up as leaders join mining rally.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up as leaders join mining rally.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed Wednesday with strong gains and heavy volumes as leading stocks joined in a rally generally evident this month only in mining companies, brokers said.
But after such strong rises, players were wary of possible technical corrections Thursday, they added.

Wednesday, the General Index rose 3.51 percent to 1,968.5 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 3.52 percent to 2,890.1 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close at 1330 local time (1830 GMT).
In a total of 2,760 trades, volume was 60.0 million soles ($22.6 million), more than double that of recent sessions, brokers said.

Polymetallic miners such as Atacocha, Morococha, Milpo, and Perubar continued their trend this month of strong volumes and high rises. But other blue chip companies which have seen relatively thin trade recently also caught fire.
The biggest gain in non-mining stocks was by Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA, which suddenly jumped in late trade.
As the session's most heavily traded share, Backus closed 7.41 percent higher at 2.32 soles in volume of 1.9 million shares.

"The Backus shares were definitely way below market value -- just like most of the industrial sector -- as the company has strong (growth) potential in the medium-term," Eder Egusquiza of local brokerage Finanval said.
Morococha rose 10.08 percent to 6.66 soles on volume of 1.6 million shares, while Atacocha jumped 10.26 percent to 2.15 soles on volume of 1.7 milion shares.
Mainly due to elevated zinc prices these two miners have led the sector's bull run all month.

But the record rally also led up Wednesday second-tier polymetal miners Milpo, which gained 10.07 percent to 30.57 soles on volume of 57,000 shares, and Perubar, which climbed 6.98 percent to 7.05 soles on volume of 390,000 shares.
